strengths: Well-motivated practical problem addressing sequential inefficiency in AR image generation with solid technical solution via guided decoding framework
Comprehensive experimental evaluation across multiple benchmarks, extensive baseline comparisons, and thorough ablation studies demonstrating technical rigor
Significant practical efficiency gains (20x throughput increase, 75% memory reduction) with competitive quality metrics, providing real-world utility
Versatile framework supporting multiple tasks: class-conditional generation, controllable generation (inpainting/outpainting/editing), zero-shot inference, and resolution expansion
Clear mathematical formulation of reformulated autoregressive modeling with decoupled positional and content guidance enabling arbitrary generation orders
Detailed ablation studies (Tables 5-7) systematically exploring decoder design, generation order effects, and efficiency-quality tradeoffs
weaknesses: Limited conceptual novelty: core contribution of using positional embeddings for generation order guidance is incremental; insufficient differentiation from concurrent RandAR work [25]
Evaluation limited to 256×256 and 512×512 resolutions; no testing at higher resolutions (768×1024), limiting assessment of scalability for modern applications
Weak theoretical justification for why random-order generation maintains quality comparable to sequential generation; limited mechanistic understanding of why this works
No human evaluation results despite claiming high-quality synthesis; relies solely on FID/IS metrics with known limitations; missing diversity metrics (precision/recall)
Incomplete comparison with most relevant baseline: RandAR [25] receives minimal detailed analysis despite addressing the same problem of random-order generation

Fair comparison concerns: different baselines trained on different data/settings with unclear hyperparameter tuning equivalence; strong claims about [MASK] tokens supported primarily by empirical evidence
Limited reproducibility: no code/model release mentioned, missing optimizer details, no hyperparameter sensitivity analysis, unknown generalization to datasets beyond ImageNet-1K
Controllable generation tasks (inpainting, outpainting) evaluated only qualitatively without quantitative metrics; zero-shot generalization to unseen classes unclear
Presentation issues: notation inconsistencies (⊙ operator), unclear relationship between 2-pass decoder design and core contribution, inconsistent figure quality

strengths: Comprehensive experimental evaluation with extensive ablations on ImageNet-1K at multiple resolutions, providing thorough empirical characterization
Demonstrates versatility across multiple tasks (class-conditional, controllable generation, inpainting, outpainting, resolution expansion) within a single framework
Clean conceptual framework decoupling positional guidance from content representation, with implementation details and pseudocode provided for reproducibility
Technically sound approach combining random-order modeling with guided decoding to enable parallel inference
Competitive FID/IS scores on ImageNet-1K 256×256 benchmark compared to contemporary methods
weaknesses: Limited novelty: core contribution combines existing techniques (random-order modeling, masked tokens, standard attention mechanisms) without significant theoretical innovation or insights

Overstated efficiency claims: claimed '20-fold throughput increase' misleading as it conflates step counts; per-step throughput improvements are modest (~2x), and memory savings are expected consequences of fewer decoding steps rather than algorithmic innovations
Modest and inconsistent empirical improvements: FID 2.44 vs competitors achieving 2.53-2.61; Table 7 shows random order marginally outperforms fixed orders (2.49 vs 2.44), undermining central claims
Narrow evaluation scope: limited to ImageNet-1K only, no evaluation on COCO or other domains; no human perceptual quality studies; missing comparisons with recent efficient generation methods

Insufficient technical justification: why random-order generation improves quality is unclear; lack of analysis on what positional information is learned; limited ablations on design choices; Equations 8-10 reformulation lacks theoretical grounding
Weak controllable generation section: underdeveloped treatment of inpainting/outpainting/resolution expansion with limited quantitative comparisons to specialized methods
Inconsistent results across resolutions: achieves FID 3.38 at 512×512 (worse than several baselines); some experimental choices questionable (fine-tuning from 256×256 pretraining)
Missing important analysis: no failure case analysis, diversity metrics (precision/recall), mode collapse discussion, or statistical significance testing with error bars

strengths: Novel and elegant core contribution: Decoupling position guidance from content representation enables random-order token generation, overcoming fundamental limitations of sequential autoregressive models
Strong technical execution with sound mathematical formulation: Guided decoding framework (Eqs. 8-12) is well-designed and properly implements parallel attention mechanisms with causal consistency

Comprehensive experimental evaluation: Extensive baselines (15+ methods including recent SOTA like VAR, RandAR), rigorous ablation studies (Table 5), multiple metrics (FID, IS, Precision, Recall), and proper evaluation protocol on standard benchmarks
Significant practical efficiency gains: 20× throughput improvement and 75% memory reduction while maintaining competitive generation quality demonstrate real deployment value
Demonstrated versatility: Zero-shot support for inpainting, outpainting, and resolution expansion shows method generality beyond standard generation
Clear presentation and reproducibility: Well-written paper with effective visualizations, pseudo-code provided, comprehensive implementation details, and good motivation through key insights
weaknesses: Limited evaluation scope: Restricted to class-conditional ImageNet generation at moderate resolutions (256×256, 512×512); no text-to-image evaluation despite this being the dominant paradigm, significantly limiting broader impact

Incomplete theoretical analysis: While intuitive insights motivate the approach, deeper theoretical understanding of why random order maintains quality is lacking; no formal convergence or optimality analysis
Modest quality improvements: FID gains over existing methods (VAR, RandAR) are marginal; efficiency improvements are the main contribution rather than generation quality

Insufficient zero-shot task evaluation: Inpainting/outpainting results shown only qualitatively (Figure 5) without quantitative comparison to specialized methods; claims about zero-shot capabilities lack comprehensive benchmarking

Incomplete efficiency analysis: Actual wall-clock inference time not reported; memory reduction baseline and detailed breakdown unclear; shared KV cache shows quality degradation in Table 5 with insufficient discussion of trade-offs
Limited architectural generality: Demonstrated only with one specific 2-pass decoder architecture; claims of model-agnosticism would be stronger with evidence across different base architectures

Generation order analysis incomplete: Table 7 shows significant variation across orders with limited guidance on selection strategy and incomplete explanation for poor performance of certain orders (Z-curve, Spiral)
No code availability mentioned: Limits reproducibility and future research building on this work

strengths: Well-motivated approach addressing genuine efficiency limitations of sequential AR models with elegant two-pass decoding mechanism
Strong empirical results: 30× speedup, 75% memory reduction, and competitive FID (1.83) on ImageNet-256
Comprehensive experimental evaluation across multiple tasks (class-conditional, text-to-image, controllable, zero-shot generation) with thorough ablation studies
Insightful empirical analysis including attention visualization (Fig. 3) showing how masked tokens dominate, supporting key design choices
Clear presentation with effective figures, detailed pseudo-code (Appendix E), and thorough implementation details for reproducibility
Versatility demonstrated across diverse generation tasks without task-specific tuning
weaknesses: Limited core novelty—individual components (two-pass decoding, separate attention queries/keys) are established techniques; core insight about masked modeling inefficiency is relatively straightforward
Incomplete baseline comparisons—limited evaluation against other recent parallel AR methods beyond RandAR; missing wall-clock time comparisons; no recent diffusion baselines
Shallow theoretical contribution—Appendix C proof is elementary application of chain rule; lacks rigor and depth compared to empirical claims
Narrow evaluation scope—primarily ImageNet; text-to-image uses limited metrics (no CLIP, LLAVA, human eval); zero-shot tasks are simple without quantitative evaluation
Missing important analyses of failure modes, limitations, and when random-order decoding provides benefits versus hurts; KV cache overhead not quantified separately
Incremental novelty and modest conceptual advancement; while practically useful, the work lacks groundbreaking insights or transformative contributions to the field

strengths: Well-motivated problem addressing genuine limitations of traditional autoregressive models in efficiency and generalization

Comprehensive experimental evaluation spanning class-conditional generation, controllable generation, and zero-shot tasks with strong empirical results (FID 1.83 at 32 steps on ImageNet-1K, 30× speedup)
Thorough ablation studies systematically examining architecture choices, decoder proportions, and design decisions
Clear presentation with good visualizations of the two-pass decoder architecture and mathematical formulation
Demonstrated versatility across diverse generation tasks (inpainting, outpainting, resolution expansion, text-to-image)
weaknesses: Limited technical novelty: decoupling content from position via two-pass decoding is a straightforward engineering solution rather than a fundamental algorithmic advance
Critical missing baseline: RandAR (Pang et al., 2025) also claims random-order parallel generation but lacks thorough direct comparison—this should be a primary baseline

Weak theoretical justification: Key Insights 1-3 are informal observations rather than rigorous arguments; Appendix C proof is limited in scope and doesn't validate the necessity of the proposed two-pass design

Marginal empirical benefit of core claim: Table 7 shows random-order generation provides only 3.6% improvement over raster order (287.1 vs 277.0 Recall), questioning whether the architectural complexity is justified
Insufficient evaluation of zero-shot generalization: qualitative results in Figure 8 lack quantitative benchmarks on standard tasks (COCO inpainting, BSD restoration, etc.)
Efficiency claims focus on sampling steps rather than actual wall-clock time or hardware latency; the two-pass architecture's practical speedup is unclear
No exploration of simpler alternatives: ablations don't compare against unified single-pass architectures or simpler position guidance mechanisms
Text-to-image evaluation limited to 4M subset of BLIP-3α; unclear if improvements generalize to full-scale settings

strengths: Clear and well-motivated contribution: Identifies genuine limitations of existing AR models (order constraints, training inefficiency, attention redundancy) and proposes a principled solution through decoupled two-pass decoding
Strong empirical results: Achieves FID 1.83 on ImageNet-1K with 32 steps (30× speedup vs. LlamaDen), 75% memory reduction vs. VAR, while maintaining or improving generation quality

Comprehensive experimental evaluation: Thorough ablations, multiple generation tasks (class-conditional, text-to-image, controllable, zero-shot), attention visualization, and scalability analysis across model sizes
Excellent reproducibility: Detailed implementation details, hyperparameters, architecture specifications, theoretical proof in appendices, and PyTorch pseudo-code provided
Technically sound: Correct mathematical formulation, well-justified two-pass architecture, valid theoretical analysis of masked modeling inefficiency in Appendix C
Strong presentation: Well-organized paper with effective visualizations and logical progression from motivation through methodology to experiments
Versatile applicability: Successfully demonstrated across diverse generation tasks (controllable generation, inpainting, editing, zero-shot inference) indicating robust generalization
weaknesses: Limited core novelty: The two-pass decoder concept is relatively straightforward given the problem; decoupling queries to attend KV cache is an incremental architectural modification

Incomplete comparative analysis: Comparisons with different model sizes/training data, missing some recent parallel decoding methods, and the claimed 30× speedup is specific to LlamaDen comparison; speedup varies across baselines
Insufficient evaluation metrics: Relies primarily on FID/IS without perceptual metrics or human evaluation; text-to-image evaluation is limited with few baselines
Limited exploration of design choices: RoPE justification is weak, ablation on position encoding impact is missing, KV cache interaction with random ordering needs deeper explanation
Training efficiency underanalyzed: Inference efficiency is well-documented but training cost comparisons are limited; no detailed wall-clock training time comparisons
Narrow experimental scope: Evaluation primarily on natural images (ImageNet, BLIP-3o); limited exploration on artistic/sketch domains or high-resolution images
Insufficient practical analysis: Memory reduction claimed but not deeply analyzed; no discussion of hardware requirements, deployment considerations, or failure cases
